title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Malaysia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Malaysia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Malaysia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a Malaysian citizen living in Malaysia is navigating a serious or life-limiting illness, putting medical, financial, and estate-planning records in place while decision-making capacity remains intact protects both the ill person's autonomy and family administration. Under Malaysian law, advance care planning operates primarily through clinical guidance rather than standalone living-will legislation, and ordinary powers of attorney cease once a donor is adjudged mentally incapacitated. This checklist outlines verified administrative, healthcare, and legal planning steps across Malaysian statutes and public institutions [1][3][4].

steps.title: Palliative care, hospital coordination, and medical coverage
steps.html:
• National Palliative Care framework: Request a referral to a hospital palliative care unit or recognized community hospice network operating under the National Palliative Care Policy and Strategic Plan 2019-2030 issued by Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) [1].
  • Private insurance and MyKad medical records: Gather active medical insurance policies, employer panel coverage details, MyKad, and hospital registration numbers so specialist clinics and inpatient wards can verify benefits smoothly [1][2].
  • Medication and home-care preparation: Confirm home-care nursing support, controlled pain-medication prescriptions, and emergency contact protocols with the treating clinical team before transitioning care to the home [1].

steps.title: Advance care planning and treatment preferences
steps.html:
• MOH Advance Care Planning (ACP) guidance: Discuss goals of care, resuscitation preferences, and preferred care setting with doctors using the clinical Advance Care Planning Guide published by Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) [2].
  • Legal status of living wills in Malaysia: Malaysia has not enacted a standalone Advance Medical Directive statute, so written advance care plans guide clinical and family decision-making as documented clinical preferences rather than automatically binding legal commands; active euthanasia and assisted dying remain unlawful [2].
  • Appointing a family spokesperson: Record the primary family spokesperson and emergency decision contact clearly in the treating hospital's medical notes while the patient can confirm those instructions directly [2].

steps.title: Financial mandates, Powers of Attorney, and Mental Health Act 2001
steps.html:
• Registering a Power of Attorney: Under the Powers of Attorney Act 1949 (Act 424), a Power of Attorney must be authenticated and deposited with the High Court Registry to be legally valid for banking or property transactions [3].
  • Limitation on mental incapacity: Under Section 5 of Act 424, an ordinary Power of Attorney terminates if the donor is adjudged of unsound mind (unlike irrevocable powers given for valuable consideration under Section 6 or fixed-time Section 7 clauses), because Malaysia does not yet have a statutory Lasting Power of Attorney framework [3].
  • Court Committee fallback if capacity is lost: If the ill person loses capacity without ongoing property authority, Part X (Sections 56 to 72) of the Mental Health Act 2001 (Act 615) requires relatives to apply to the High Court to appoint a Committee of the person and estate, so arranging bank mandates and bill payments early reduces interim disruption [4].

steps.title: Provident fund incapacitation withdrawal and SOCSO benefits
steps.html:
• EPF / KWSP Incapacitation Withdrawal: Members under retirement age who are certified permanently physically or mentally incapacitated and unable to work may apply at a branch of Employees Provident Fund (KWSP / EPF) for full withdrawal of their retirement savings under the Incapacitation Withdrawal scheme (Form KWSP 9L) after medical board assessment [5].
  • SOCSO / PERKESO Invalidity Pension: Insured contributors under age 60 experiencing severe and permanent qualifying incapacity may apply to Social Security Organisation (PERKESO / SOCSO) for an Invalidity Pension (Pencen Ilat), Invalidity Grant, or Constant Attendance Allowance subject to medical board certification and contribution conditions [6].
  • Medical and employment leave coordination: Check Employment Act medical leave entitlements and private critical-illness insurance claims alongside statutory PERKESO assessments so documentation is filed concurrently [6].

steps.title: Nominations, wills, Faraid considerations, and cross-border records
steps.html:
• Register or update EPF nominations early: Register or verify beneficiaries with Employees Provident Fund (KWSP / EPF) via the i-Akaun mobile e-KYC flow or Form KWSP 4 with thumbprint verification; for non-Muslims, an EPF nomination overrides a will and transfers benefits directly, while for Muslim members, a nominee acts strictly as wasi (administrator) bound by Faraid distribution [5].
  • Draft a compliant will and verify dual-system rules: Non-Muslims should sign a witnessed written will complying with Section 5 of the Wills Act 1959 (Act 346) (whereas intestacy follows Distribution Act 1958 [Act 300] or Small Estates Act 1955 [Act 98] via Department of Director General of Lands and Mines (JKPTG) or summary movable administration via Amanah Raya Berhad (AmanahRaya)); Muslim residents should review Islamic Wasiat limits and Faraid heirs before Syariah Court administration is needed [7][8][9][10].
  • Consular legalization for foreign assets: Because Malaysia is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, notarized documents or powers intended for overseas use require attestation by Ministry of Foreign Affairs Malaysia (Wisma Putra) and legalization by the relevant foreign embassy or high commission [11][12].

prefillQuestion: A family member is facing a serious or terminal illness in Malaysia. We need an overview of the main official steps and contacts in Malaysia for palliative care, powers of attorney, advance directives, and caregiver support.

contacts.name: Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH)
contacts.note: Publishes the National Palliative Care Policy and Strategic Plan 2019-2030 and the clinical Advance Care Planning Guide.

contacts.name: Employees Provident Fund (KWSP / EPF)
contacts.note: Administers member nominations (Form KWSP 4 / i-Akaun) and Incapacitation Withdrawal claims.

contacts.name: Social Security Organisation (PERKESO / SOCSO)
contacts.note: Administers Invalidity Pension, Invalidity Grant, and Constant Attendance Allowance claims.

contacts.name: Amanah Raya Berhad (AmanahRaya)
contacts.note: Malaysia's public trustee providing will writing, custody, trust services, and movable estate administration.

contacts.name: Department of Director General of Lands and Mines (JKPTG)
contacts.note: Administers small-estate immovable property distribution rules under the Small Estates (Distribution) Act 1955.

contacts.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Malaysia (Wisma Putra)
contacts.note: Consular Division providing attestation for Malaysian documents used overseas in the absence of Apostille membership.
